title: Email professor for a 3-day extension
scenario: You missed the paper deadline by a day, dengue, you actually had it, but you also missed two earlier deadlines this semester (without dengue). You need a 3-day extension. The professor is fair but won't tolerate excuse-stacking. You want an email that's short, owns the prior misses without grovelling, makes one specific ask (3 days), and proposes a concrete way to make up for it. No ‘I deeply apologise for any inconvenience caused’.
badPrompt: write an email asking my professor for an extension
badOutput:
Dear Professor,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to request an extension on my recent paper. Due to unforeseen circumstances, I was unable to complete the assignment on time. I deeply apologise for any inconvenience and would greatly appreciate your understanding.

Warm regards,
Shaurya

hints.title: Ban the corporate-grovel phrases
hints.body: ‘No ‘deeply apologise’, no ‘any inconvenience’, no ‘unforeseen circumstances’.’ Professors recognise these as filler instantly.

hints.title: Acknowledge the prior misses honestly
hints.body: ‘Mention the previous misses briefly, take ownership.’ Hiding them reads worse than acknowledging.

checks.tip: Anchor the ask, a 3-day extension on a paper.
Surface the prior misses honestly, that's the politically loaded part.
Force one specific ask, 3 days, not vague ‘some extension’.
Demand a concrete make-up offer, attend extra office hours, etc.
Force a respectful + direct tone, no grovelling, no entitlement.
Specify the structure, subject line + greeting + body + sign-off.

tipIfLow: Extension emails fail when they lean on corporate grovelling. The unlock is banning the cliché phrases (‘deeply apologise’, ‘any inconvenience’), forcing a specific ask (3 days), AND owning the prior misses. Honesty + brevity beats theatre + length.
goldPrompt: Act as a writing partner who knows professors detect filler. I'm Shaurya, 4th-year liberal arts. I missed yesterday's paper deadline — dengue, real, but I also missed two earlier deadlines this term WITHOUT dengue. Need a 3-day extension. Banned phrases: 'deeply apologise', 'any inconvenience', 'unforeseen circumstances', 'hope this finds you well'. Output an email under 120 words that: (1) names the situation in one line, (2) acknowledges the prior misses honestly without grovelling, (3) asks for exactly 3 days (specific date), (4) proposes one concrete way to make up for the pattern. Subject line included.
